title: How to Stop a Drafty Door Without Replacing the Whole Door
description: A practical way to find the leak, choose the right seal and avoid spending money where the real problem is somewhere else.
image_alt: Front door in a bright home entryway
body_html:
A cold strip of air around a door can make a room feel uncomfortable and can push you toward an expensive replacement you may not need. Start by finding exactly where the air is getting through.

1. Find the leak before buying anything

On a windy day, move your hand slowly around the closed door, especially along the hinge side, latch side and bottom edge. You can also use a thin piece of tissue paper: movement points to an air path. Check the frame as well as the door itself.

2. Check the seal first

If the gap is between the moving door and the frame, a compression weatherstrip is often the simplest fix. The seal should meet the closed door firmly without requiring excessive force to latch it.

3. Treat the bottom separately

A visible gap under the door needs a door sweep or threshold adjustment rather than more foam around the frame. Keep the sweep light enough that the door still opens normally.

4. Do not seal over a different problem

If the frame is loose, the door is badly misaligned, or the gap changes dramatically from top to bottom, the issue may be alignment rather than worn weatherstripping. Fixing the underlying movement will usually last longer.

Quick test

  • Locate the exact leak.
  • Measure the gap before buying a seal.
  • Choose frame weatherstrip for frame gaps and a sweep for bottom gaps.
  • Close the door several times after installation to check the seal.

The useful rule is simple: seal the gap you actually have, not the gap you assume you have.
